To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we can learn to estimate depth, camera and rigid motion in a video from a single RGB input, without using any depth or ground truth camera or motion supervision.
we propose a neural network that learns to predict scene and object depths, ego-motion, and object rotations and translations, from a sequence of images, and that it can do so without supervision.

we propose a novel deep learning approach to the problem of motion estimation from video that is based on a neural network that predicts depth and motion, and is able to learn from self-supervised training with photometric error.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) can we learn a single network that can predict depth, camera motion, object motion and optical flow from video?
learning a model for dense motion estimation that can be trained with different levels of supervision.
the development of a neural architecture that learns the structure and motion of a scene from video.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is able to estimate depth, motion, segmentation and camera motion, all in a self-supervised manner.
the paper proposes an unsupervised learning method for estimating camera pose and depth from a monocular sequence of frames.
the proposed SfM-Neural Network is a powerful tool that allows to estimate the 3D structure and the 3D motion of the observed scene from a video sequence, without any supervision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SfM- Net is a deep neural network that can learn the geometry of the scene and the camera from video, and it can also learn the motion of the camera and rigid objects from the scene.

the proposed SfM- Net can be trained with different levels of supervision (self-supervised, ego-motion, depth), can predict camera and rigid object motion, can be used for frame-to-frame optical flow estimation, and can extract depth maps from videos, all of which can be learned in an end-to-end manner.
SfMNet is a geometry-aware neural architecture that can estimate dense frame-to-frame optical flow from videos in a completely unsupervised manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single model can be trained end-to-end to jointly predict depth and camera motion in videos, and can be used to estimate the motion of objects in the scene.
the geometry-aware SfM-Neural network can be used to estimate the 3D scene and object structure and motion, even in the presence of occlusions and without the use of any 3D supervision.
a neural network can be trained end-to-end, in a self-supervised fashion, to learn a dense frame-toframe optical flow, camera motion and object motion, by only relying on the photometric error.
